# Citation

Haller, B. C., and Messer, P. W. (2019). *SLiM 3: Forward genetic simulations beyond the Wright-Fisher model*. Molecular Biology and Evolution. DOI: 10.1093/molbev/msy228. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6389312/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6389312/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Describes SLiM 3, a flexible forward genetic simulator that supports models beyond standard Wright-Fisher assumptions.

# Scope for simitall

Document as an advanced external engine for users who require detailed demography, selection, spatial processes, or custom life histories beyond the first simitall breeding presets.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Forward simulation can represent selection and demography in detail but needs careful parameterization.
- Non-Wright-Fisher life cycles allow more realistic individual-based models.
- Complex models benefit from independently checked summaries of diversity, LD, and demography.

# Inputs to Specify

- Genome model and mutation/recombination assumptions
- Demographic and life-history model
- Selection and migration rules

# Expected Outputs

- Tree sequences or simulated genetic data
- Population-level summaries
- Custom event records when coded

# Limitations and Guardrails

- SLiM is powerful but not a drop-in substitute for a simple breeding workflow.
- Agent plans should recommend it only when its added model complexity is justified.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- When is SLiM more appropriate than a simplified breeding simulator?
- What validation summaries should a forward population-genetics simulation report?
